fields.description:
## Context / Problem
Operator directive (2026-08-13): "The tickets branch should never trigger CI. The branch is
noisy and doesn't contain code." rebar auto-pushes the `tickets` branch to `origin` on EVERY
write (comment/edit/claim/close), so each ticket event fires the four workflows that push-
trigger on all-branches-but-two. During the 2026-08-12/13 bug bash this starved the org-wide
GitHub Actions runner pool (navapbc is on GitHub Free: 20 concurrent jobs, 5 macOS, shared
across the org), queueing a Gerrit `Verified` pytest matrix ~2 hours behind tickets-push runs.

## Approach
Audit every file in `.github/workflows/` for an `on.push` trigger. Measured today, exactly four
have one — `test.yml`, `optionality.yml`, `prompt-eval.yml`, `verify-identity.yml` — and all
four already use the SAME idiom: `branches-ignore: ["feature/**", "main"]`. The ticket's
original finding that `reconcile-bridge.yml` push-triggers is STALE: it is schedule +
`workflow_dispatch` only today. Every other workflow is `workflow_call`, `workflow_dispatch`,
`schedule`, `pull_request`, or `pull_request_target`.

So the change is minimal and idiom-preserving: append `"tickets"` to those four
`branches-ignore` lists (keeping `branches-ignore` as the ONE consistent idiom rather than
converting anything to explicit allow-lists), each with a one-line comment citing
`refractive-conceptual-sunbear`. No `schedule:` block is touched, so the replacement cadences
the directive relies on are unchanged by construction: reconcile-bridge `*/20 * * * *`,
verify-identity `53 */6 * * *`, test `41 */6 * * *`, optionality `47 */6 * * *`, prompt-eval
weekly `0 7 * * 1`.

Enforcement: the sibling policy module `tests/unit/test_ci_main_push_policy.py` already models
GitHub's branch filtering in its `_push_matches_branch` helper but only pins the four known
workflow NAMES. A future workflow added with a bare `push:` would silently regress this
invariant, so the new test module ENUMERATES every `*.yml`/`*.yaml` under `.github/workflows/`
from disk and asserts none of them push-matches `tickets`, plus that non-tickets topic-branch
push CI still fires (the scratch-branch push lane is the only pre-merge validation path for a
workflow change — the Gerrit Verified lane resolves `uses: ./.github/workflows/...` from the
default branch and therefore cannot exercise a workflow edit).

Out of scope, stated as a deliberate default: `pull_request:` filters on the BASE branch, not
the head, so a tickets-headed PR cannot be excluded by branch filter — and `lockdown.yml`
auto-closes PRs on this mirror anyway. Leave `pull_request` triggers alone.

Not changed, by operator instruction: `gerrit-verify.yaml` stays `workflow_dispatch`-only (it
is the sole `Verified` source, dispatched by Gerrit per patchset).

**Adopter documentation (operator scope addition).** This hazard is not specific to this repo:
ANY rebar adopter whose CI watches all branches turns every comment into a workflow run,
because the store auto-pushes on every write. Document it once where an adopter configures the
store's remote, and cross-link rather than triplicate. The canonical warning goes in
`docs/concurrency.md` under "Outbound — push (on every write)" (the mechanism section that
already states every write auto-pushes); `docs/user-guide.md` gets a short pointer at the "The
store **auto-pushes**" paragraph; `docs/config.md` gets a one-line pointer in the `sync.remote`
annotation. Wording is adopter guidance — "configure your CI so the tickets branch never
triggers workflows; use a schedule for anything that must read the store" — not a retelling of
this repo's incident.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` — add `"tickets"` to `on.push.branches-ignore` + citation comment.
- `.github/workflows/optionality.yml` — same.
- `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml` — same.
- `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml` — same.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_push_policy.py` — NEW: the enumerate-all-workflows invariant.
- `docs/concurrency.md` — canonical adopter warning in the outbound-push section.
- `docs/user-guide.md` — short pointer at the auto-push/comment paragraph.
- `docs/config.md` — one-line pointer in the `sync.remote` annotation.

## Testing
- Happy path: for each workflow file discovered on disk, a push to `tickets` does not match its
  `on.push` filter (a workflow with no `push` key trivially passes).
- Regression/edge: a hypothetical `on: push:` with NO branch filter, and one with
  `branches: [tickets]`, are both classified as matching by the shared filter model, so the
  enumerating test would fail if such a workflow were added later.
- Preserved-behaviour path: the four edited workflows still push-match an ordinary topic branch
  (`wip-some-topic`) and still skip `feature/**` and `main`.
- Schedule path: each edited workflow's cron list is asserted unchanged against its literal.
- Live end-to-end (post-merge, AC2): make a trivial rebar write (a comment on this ticket),
  capture the resulting `tickets` head SHA, then query
  `/repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs?branch=tickets` and confirm zero runs exist for that SHA.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] No file in `.github/workflows/` triggers on a push to `tickets` — checked by the new
      enumerating test, which reads the directory rather than a hard-coded name list, so an
      added workflow cannot regress it silently.
- [x] A tickets-branch push made AFTER the change merges produces zero new workflow runs —
      checked by the GitHub Actions API for that push's head SHA, evidence recorded as a
      comment on this ticket.
- [x] Every `schedule:` cron in the repo is byte-identical to its pre-change value — checked by
      `git diff` showing no change inside any `schedule:` block, and by the cron literals
      asserted in the new test (reconcile-bridge `*/20 * * * *` and verify-identity
      `53 */6 * * *` explicitly).
- [x] `gerrit-verify.yaml` remains `workflow_dispatch`-only — checked by the existing
      `test_gerrit_verify_stays_a_dispatch_only_patchset_gate` in
      `tests/unit/test_ci_main_push_policy.py` still passing.
- [x] Push CI for ordinary topic branches is preserved — checked by the new test asserting
      `wip-some-topic` still matches all four edited workflows.
- [x] Client-facing docs warn adopters against CI triggered by tickets-branch pushes — checked
      by `grep` finding the warning in `docs/concurrency.md` (canonical, naming the schedule
      alternative) and a cross-link to it in both `docs/user-guide.md` and `docs/config.md`,
      with the guidance phrased for any adopter rather than as this repo's incident report.
- [x] Full local gate set green (ten `check_*` gates, generators no-diff, `make lint`,
      `make typecheck`, CI-equivalent pytest tier) and the change lands with `LLM-Review +1`
      and `Verified +1`.
